title: Sphinx: A High-Performance Hybrid Index for Disaggregated Memory With Succinct Filter Cache
problem: Range indexes for disaggregated memory architectures suffer from excessive network round trips during tree traversal and inefficient node-based caching, limiting lookup performance for variable-length keys.
motivation: Disaggregated memory architectures promise better resource utilization, but existing indexes cannot efficiently exploit the network-centric design.
method: Sphinx speeds up lookups by replacing sequential tree navigation—where you ask about one branch at a time and wait for each answer—with parallel hash reads. It uses an Inner Node Hash Table to check multiple branches at once, cutting down network round trips. A Succinct Filter Cache on the computing side further reduces network traffic by keeping track of which remote data locations are likely to contain your target, staying small and coherent.
key_novelty: An Inner Node Hash Table replaces sequential tree traversal (checking one branch at a time) with parallel hash lookups, eliminating network bottlenecks.
contributions: Inner Node Hash Table that converts sequential tree traversal to parallel hash reads, reducing network round trips
Succinct Filter Cache that minimizes network overhead while maintaining cache coherence and small footprint
Demonstrated 7.3× speedup on YCSB benchmark over state-of-the-art indexes
limitations: Evaluation limited to YCSB benchmark; generalization to other workloads not discussed.
